hints: Notice the string is below the wooden block and attached to the bottom, so its tension pulls downward on the block while the block is stated to be stationary.
Connect the displaced water of volume $V$ and density $\rho$ to the upward Archimedes upthrust $\rho gV$, with downward weight $mg$.
Write vertical equilibrium for zero resultant force with upthrust upward balancing weight plus tension downward, then rearrange for tension.
walkthrough: Identify the three vertical forces on the block: weight $mg$ downward, tension $T$ downward from the string below, and upthrust upward from the water.
State the upthrust rule: upthrust equals weight of displaced fluid, so $U = \rho V g$ upward because the block displaces volume $V$ of water of density $\rho$.
Use equilibrium because the block is held stationary, so resultant force is zero and upward force equals total downward force: $\rho gV = mg + T$.
Rearrange for the tension magnitude: $T = \rho gV - mg$.

options.A: This is only the upthrust $\rho gV$ acting upward on volume $V$. It ignores the downward weight $mg$ that also acts on the stationary block.
options.B: Adding $mg + \rho gV$ would treat weight and upthrust as acting in the same direction. They act in opposite directions on the block.
options.C: This is only the weight $mg$ acting downward. It ignores the upward upthrust from the displaced water.
options.D: Upward upthrust $\rho gV$ balances downward weight $mg$ plus downward tension $T$, so $T = \rho gV - mg$.
